messages:
incident-bot: Paging on-call: ALB/NLB 5xx spike in eu-west-1 affecting Redwood hosted API (route: /v1/generate). Alert: 5xx-rate 21% over last 5m; error pattern: connection_reset / upstream_reset. Auto-fallback not triggered.

marta: on it. seeing the same in dashboards. 5xx started ~ 03:42 UTC. I’m pulling ELB metrics and ingress logs now.

devon: I can take a look at ingress. Are we sure this is ALB vs NLB? logs show both ALB 502/504 and envoy upstream resets.

marta: good q — initial suspicion is ALB -> targets failing healthchecks, then traffic flips to another AZ causing resets. but envoy also shows `upstream reset` on application connections.

prateek: copying recent deploys — no infra deploys in last 6 hours. application deploys none. only config change was autoscaling rule tweak yesterday.

eli: customer-impact calc: hosted API request volume that hits eu-west-1 is ~18% of global. given 21% 5xx, rough affected user requests ~3.8% of total platform traffic. high for SLOs.

marta: mitigation plan: 1) stop routing new traffic to the failing AZ by setting ALB AZ enablement (drain) 2) increase ALB connection timeout 3) restart envoy-ingress in the affected k8s nodes 4) adjust target group healthcheck grace. doing step 1 now.

marta: running: 
```bash
# disable AZ (manual step via CLI)
aws elbv2 set-subnets --load-balancer-arn $ALB_ARN --subnets <subnets-for-remaining-azs> --region eu-west-1
```

devon: FYI I’m tailing envoy logs for 10.0.2.* nodes. found repeated "upstream connection reset by peer" for target ip 10.0.2.45:8080. That pod is in availability zone b.

prateek: checking target group health: 
```text
Target 10.0.2.45:8080 -> Unhealthy, last_failed_health_check=3, code=502
```

eli: support-bot FYI — opening incident page for customers to track. 

support-bot: Incident page created: https://status.redwood.example/incidents/INC-2026-127-eu-lb (auto).

marta: after removing AZ-b from ALB subnets traffic returned to normal for a subset, 5xx dropped from 21% to ~6% in 4m. still seeing occasional resets. continuing with envoy restart.

devon: performing controlled restart of envoy-ingress (k8s):
```bash
kubectl -n ingress rollout restart deployment/envoy-ingress --selector=zone=b
```

devon: restart succeeded on 3 pods in zone b. post-restart checks: envoy upstream resets dropped but we're still seeing elevated 502s for long-running connections. could be keepalive/socket reuse issue with ALB.

prateek: suggest toggling ALB target group attribute `deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds` and `stickiness` off for canary. running command to reduce drain time to 10s to speed failover: 
```bash
aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes --target-group-arn $TG_ARN --attributes Key=deregistration_delay.timeout_seconds,Value=10 --region eu-west-1
```

marta: applied. also increased ALB idle timeout from 60 -> 120 to accommodate longer requests (they were being cut mid-stream). command: 
```bash
aws elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-arn $ALB_ARN --attributes Key=idle_timeout.timeout_seconds,Value=120
```

eli: monitoring: 5xx now trending to ~1.8% overall in the region. latency bump of ~80ms as traffic moved to other AZs. Noted customer-facing impact: brief errors for some streaming/streaming-like requests.

marta: coordinating with networking — they are checking cross-AZ networking between eu-west-1a and eu-west-1b. preliminary note: packet drops on a couple of ToR switches earlier at ~03:35 UTC.

june: quick note for postmortem: collect ALB access logs + envoy/access + kube events for 03:30-04:15 UTC. we'll need to map unhealthy targets -> switch logs -> pod restarts.

devon: done a shallow root-cause hypothesis: intermittent switch-level packet drops caused target health flaps -> ALB reroutes -> Envoy connection resets on in-flight requests. remediation: 1) drain failing AZ (done) 2) restart envoy pods (done) 3) temporary ALB timeouts/attributes tweaked (done) 4) recommend long-term: adjust healthcheck thresholds and enable cross-zone load balancing affinity.

marta: sounds good. starting incident severity summary for SRE/ops:
- severity: Sev2 (partial outage degraded for eu-west-1 hosted API)
- start: 2026-03-11T03:42:01Z (approx)
- scope: ~18% regional traffic, ~21% 5xx at peak -> ~3.8% of global requests impacted
- mitigation: drained AZ-b from ALB, restarted envoy, adjusted TG/ALB attributes
- current status: degraded -> recovering (5xx ~1.8%, latency +80ms)

eli: informing growth + support: please post incident page update with mitigation and customer advice to retry and fallback to other regions if configured.

support-bot: Status page updated with current mitigation steps.

marta: handing off to devon for next 4h monitoring window. devon, you have the on-call. i’ll stay nearby for escalation.

devon: taking over monitoring. will watch dashboards and correlation logs. if 5xx >5% again will escalate to networking and open AWS support ticket.

marta: extra follow-up actions added to postmortem checklist: 
- capture packet-drop logs from ToR at 03:30-03:50
- correlate with ALB access logs and pod-level metrics
- review healthcheck thresholds and reduce sensitivity to brief network blips
- add automated fallback to cross-region for critical routes

devon: noted. thanks team. :thumbsup:

marta: closing thread for now — will reopen if we see re-regression. final last_message_ts updated.
